claims.text: The as-printed Al0.2Co1.5CrFeNi1.5Ti0.3 alloy is more than 97% dense.
The as-printed alloy has a single-FCC cellular microstructure.
Cr is uniformly distributed in the as-printed alloy.
Aging at 750°C for 50 h produces approximately 25–30 vol% dual nanoprecipitates.
The aged alloy contains Ni/Ti-enriched L12 nanoprecipitates.
The aged alloy contains Al/Ti-enriched L21 nanoprecipitates.
Formation of the dual nanoprecipitates causes heterogeneous Cr distribution and localized Cr-depleted regions near precipitate–matrix boundaries.
Nanoprecipitation introduces additional matrix–precipitate interfaces.
The additional matrix–precipitate interfaces may act as short-circuit diffusion paths for oxygen.
Initial oxidation in both as-printed and aged states forms loose or discontinuous oxides.
Uniform Cr distribution in the as-printed alloy enables rapid formation of a continuous Cr2O3 scale.
The continuous Cr2O3 scale restricts further oxidation of the as-printed alloy.
Cr-depleted regions in the aged alloy delay formation of a fully protective Cr2O3 layer.
Delayed Cr2O3 formation and interface-assisted oxygen diffusion increase the oxidation rate of the aged alloy.
The aged alloy will exhibit greater oxidation mass gain than the as-printed baseline.
The difference in oxidation mass gain will be particularly pronounced above 900°C.
Once a Cr2O3 layer is established, the aged and as-printed states will have similar high-temperature oxide-growth activation energies.
Below approximately 900°C, protective behavior of the Cr2O3 layer dominates oxidation behavior.
Above approximately 900°C, limited Cr availability in the aged alloy becomes increasingly influential.
The proposed behavior is expected to hold during isothermal exposure from 600°C to 1200°C for up to 96 h.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis predicts similar activation energies after establishment of Cr2O3, but the falsification rule says indistinguishable kinetics, including activation energies, would reject the hypothesis. Similar activation energies are therefore presented as both a prediction and a potential falsifier.
